problems.quote: This symmetry, on an interval, often forces f ′ to be constant ±1, leading to f ( x ) = x or f ( x ) = c − x .
problems.problem: The claim that a differentiable involution on an interval must have constant derivative ±1 is false; counterexample: f(x)=1/x on (0,∞) is an involution with f'(x)=-1/x^2.
problems.correction: This symmetry implies f'(f(x)) f'(x)=1, but f' need not be constant; e.g., f(x)=1/x on (0,∞).
problems.verifierReason: Quote incorrectly states involution forces constant derivative ±1; correction gives true derivative identity and valid counterexample f(x)=1/x.
